html:
The Yuezhi were a nomadic herding people who, in the first millennium BCE, lived in the grasslands of what is now western Gansu in China. The map shows them around 200 BCE.

They were strong until the Xiongnu rose against them. After a heavy defeat in 176 BCE most Yuezhi moved far west, first to the Ili valley and then, pushed on by the Wusun, south to the Oxus and Bactria. A smaller group, the Lesser Yuezhi, stayed near the Qilian Mountains. Their move set off a chain of migrations that drove the Saka into Iran and India.

The Han envoy Zhang Qian reached them around 128 BCE, hoping for an alliance against the Xiongnu, but they had settled down and refused. Within a century one of their five clans, the Kushans, united the others and founded the Kushan Empire. Some scholars link the Yuezhi with the speakers of the Tocharian languages.
